name: Chulyshman Valley and Katu-Yaryk Pass
full: The Chulyshman River valley (the lower ≈75 km from the pass to Lake Teletskoye) and the Katu-Yaryk road descent/serpentine — the only overland entry into the valley, Ulagan district
near: From above — Balyktuyul village (≈30 km to the pass) and Ulagan village (≈47 km); in the valley — Koo village and Balykcha village (by Lake Teletskoye)
elev: Top of the pass / viewpoint ≈1200 m; bottom of the serpentine ≈670 m; drop ≈500–600 m (530 m according to some sources); valley floor at the lake 400–450 m
short: A deep Chulyshman canyon with sheer walls, waterfalls and the Stone Mushrooms, reached via the famous Katu-Yaryk — 3.5–3.9 km of serpentine with nine hairpins and a gradient of up to 70%.
desc: The Chulyshman is the main river feeding Lake Teletskoye (241 km). Tourists can reach the lower ≈75 km of the valley — from the foot of Katu-Yaryk Pass to the south shore of Lake Teletskoye. The valley is cut about a kilometer below the surrounding plateaus, so it has its own warm microclimate: in summer about +18 °C and higher, and apricots, pears and grapes were historically grown in the valley (by monks in the late 19th century). Telengits live here, and wooden churches stand in the villages of Koo and Balykcha. The Katu-Yaryk descent was built by bulldozer operators in 1987–1989 on the initiative of the state-farm director A. V. Sanaa; before that the valley could be reached only by the lake or on horse trails. The serpentine is 3.5–3.9 km long with 7–9 steep hairpins, single-lane, with passing pockets, and a slope of about 35° (70%). From the upper viewpoint you can see the canyon, the river and an almost 100 m waterfall on the opposite wall. In March 2026 construction of a new two-lane descent to the left of the current one was announced (≈4.9 billion ₽, due at the end of October 2027). The valley has the Kurkure (≈30 m), Uchar (≈160 m) and Achelman (near Balykcha) waterfalls, the Ak-Kurum Stone Mushrooms, and dozens of tourist bases and campsites. There is no grid electricity or stable mobile signal: generators and solar panels, and in Balykcha the Kayru mini-hydropower plant.
guide: Walk Katu-Yaryk on foot as far as the first hairpin first — from the top you will see the whole canyon and the waterfall on the opposite wall. If you're driving, descend in low gear and don't brake in the turns, and take a run-up for the climb in advance; if you can't make it, the tourist bases below will tow you out with a tractor for a fee. There are no cafes or shops in the valley, so stock up in Ulagan. And don't rush: Telengits live here, and in the evenings fishermen go out on the Chulyshman for grayling.
see: The viewpoint on Katu-Yaryk (≈1200 m) and the serpentine itself; Kurkure waterfall (≈30 m, requires a crossing of the Chulyshman); Karasu waterfall (≈40 m); the Ak-Kurum Stone Mushrooms; Uchar waterfall (17 km hike); Achelman waterfall near Balykcha; the wooden churches in Koo and Balykcha; Cape Kyrsay and the mouth of the Chulyshman on Lake Teletskoye
skip: you have a sedan or a rental car (rental companies fine you for driving Katu-Yaryk), you're afraid of heights behind the wheel, or you have less than two days — in that case the viewpoint at the top of the pass is enough
diff: For the driver — high (a steep single-lane serpentine, rocks, 4WD and high ground clearance needed); for a passenger/walker — easy to moderate (walking up and down the serpentine ≈10 km, ascent ≈580 m)
when: May to September; May — maralnik (Siberian rhododendron) in bloom, snow on the plateau; July–August — warm, but the bases are packed; September — colors (in mid-month there can be an invasion of stink bugs). In October most bases close. In winter entry is possible in a 4WD car, and winter is low on snow (January ≈ −7 °C)
hours: Open around the clock, with no barriers. Base season is usually May–September (some from 15 April to 31 October)
daytime: Morning — for the descent (fewer oncoming cars, soft light in the canyon); evening — a rainbow at Kurkure
how: Overland: Novosibirsk/Barnaul → Biysk → Gorno-Altaysk → Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway) to Aktash (≈310 km from Gorno-Altaysk, estimate) → Ulagan road: Krasnye Vorota (Red Gates, 8 km), Ulagan Pass 2080 m (26 km), Ulagan → Balyktuyul (74 km from Aktash) → ≈30 km of gravel to the pass (≈100 km from Aktash) → descent and ≈75 km along the valley to Lake Teletskoye. By water: from Artybash by ferry (5–6 h) or motorboat to the south shore, then up the valley by car/UAZ
needcar: Yes: a prepared 4×4 / SUV, a tour with a jeep/UAZ, or a ferry with your car; there is no public transport into the valley
self: Yes, in your own prepared 4×4 / SUV or by ferry with your car; without a car — only with a tour or a tourist base transfer
roadtype: Ulagan road Aktash — Ulagan — Balyktuyul: paved/gravel, under repair; Balyktuyul — pass ≈30 km of gravel with rocks; Katu-Yaryk — a single-lane rocky dirt serpentine; along the valley to Balykcha — dirt road
traveltime: Aktash → pass ≈2.5–3 h; descent ≈20–30 min; pass → Ak-Kurum ≈1 h, → Balykcha ≈2–2.5 h (estimates). Gorno-Altaysk → pass — a full day
stay: Dozens of bases (2GIS, 2026): Katu-Yaryk (km 34, from 4500 ₽, 4.6/80), Dolina Kamennykh Gribov (km 61, from 4500 ₽, 4.8/99), Dolina Vodopadov (km 61, from 3000 ₽, 4.9/67), Kamennye Griby campsite (km 61, from 2500 ₽, 4.3/79), Uchar (km 57, from 2000 ₽, 3.5/28), Zolotaya Dolina Chulyshmana (Koo, from 2500 ₽, 5.0/6), in Balykcha — Achelman (from 5000 ₽, 4.9/70), Start (from 7000 ₽, 4.4/57), Chulyshman (Cape Kyrsay, from 500 ₽, 3.9/53), the Vyshe Gor glamping (from 5000 ₽). Tents at campsites from 100 ₽/person (KP)
net: Up top at Ulagan and Balyktuyul there is a signal; below the pass there was none for a long time (KP: none), since 2024–2025 it has appeared but is unstable (T—Zh, 2025); operators not specified. Some bases have Wi-Fi via satellite
entry: Entry to the valley and the pass is free. Paid are the Altai Nature Reserve routes (Uchar; 100–250 ₽, data differ) and boat crossings. No border-zone permit needed
transfer: Car ferry 15–17k ₽, pedestrian 3000 ₽ (2026); jeep tour from Aktash ≈23,000 ₽ per car (2022) / from 38,800 ₽ per group (Tripster, 2026); tour from Artybash 12,000 ₽/person
bring: A full tank and a jerrycan (fuel stations only in Ulagan/Aktash), cash, food, a first-aid kit, a tow rope; repellent; warm clothes for the plateau and light ones for the valley
warn: Katu-Yaryk is a steep single-lane serpentine without guardrails: only 4WD, high ground clearance and experience; rental companies fine you for the trip. After rains — rockfalls and fords. There are no shops, cafes or fuel stations in the valley. Bears: in August 2026 the reserve closed the Uchar trail. Ticks (May–July). No border-zone permit needed — Ulagan district is not in the border zone. From 2026 a new descent is being built nearby — construction machinery may be at work (no traffic restrictions found in the sources)
food: Meals at the tourist bases (dinner for two from ≈1300 ₽, KP); grayling from the Chulyshman; at the top of the pass — a cafe by the viewpoint (Turister); in Ulagan and Aktash — cafes with Altai cuisine (kecheh-kasha, tutpash)
reviews: Katu-Yaryk on 2GIS — 5.0 (6 ratings). Tourist bases in the valley on 2GIS: from 3.5 to 5.0 (Dolina Vodopadov 4.9/67, Achelman 4.9/70, Dolina Kamennykh Gribov 4.8/99). Pros: wild views, warmth, few people, “one of the most impressive descents in the world”; cons: a dangerous road, spartan conditions, prices high for the level, no signal
photos.4.cap: The Chulyshman valley in late spring
p.sum: There are two ways into the Chulyshman valley: overland via Aktash, Ulagan and the Katu-Yaryk descent (≈100 km from Aktash to the pass, then ≈75 km along the valley to the lake) — only in a prepared 4×4 / SUV; or by water from Artybash by ferry (with a car 15–17k ₽, 2026) or a tour. Entry is free, no permit needed. There are no shops or fuel stations in the valley, and the signal is unstable; stay overnight at dozens of tourist bases (from 500 to 7000 ₽, 2GIS 2026). A new two-lane descent is promised by the end of October 2027.

p.season: May–September is the main season; October — the bases close; the ferry runs until early October; in winter — 4WD only, many bases closed.
p.budget.economy: ≈2500–4000 ₽/person/day: campsite 100–500 ₽, your own food, crossings 500 ₽, fuel
p.permits: No border-zone permit needed (the Altai Republic border zone covers the Kosh-Agach, Ust-Koksa and Ust-Kan districts). Registration with the Emergency Ministry (MChS) is recommended for hikes (conditions not found). Altai Nature Reserve tickets — only for its routes (Uchar).
p.access: With children and older people — on a tour or with an experienced driver; the descent is hard for people prone to motion sickness. With dogs — not specified at most bases; the ChuluCamp campsite does not accept animals.
